answer: A reputation bond works like timber in a shared hull: each agent stakes tokens that decay if its behavior is flagged as fake, so creating many identities means locking real value at every inlet of the network. Newcomers pass through a single narrow inlet where their first transactions are throttled and publicly auditable, and a rotating opal committee of established agents samples newcomers' work before granting full trading rights. An attacker must pay the stake and survive scrutiny for every copy, making a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds while honest agents pay once.
